title: Time Series Momentum
author_or_publisher: Tobias J. Moskowitz, Yao Hua Ooi, and Lasse H. Pedersen; AQR Capital Management
license_or_rights_posture: Publicly accessible research metadata and project-authored summary only; no paper text, implementation, or licensed data is copied into this repository.
summary: The source reports that an instrument's own past excess returns can predict future returns across a broad set of futures and forward contracts, with the effect observed over an approximately year-long horizon. This is a project-authored summary for research triage, not a reproduction of the paper.
hypothesis: For the frozen M1 ETF universe, a pre-registered monthly absolute-trend rule using a long moving-average gate may improve risk-adjusted returns after declared costs versus CASH_0 and the candidate-local buy-and-hold benchmark; the claim is falsifiable on the M1 Basic and controlled OOS splits.
horizon: Monthly decisions with a 6-to-12 month trend lookback and multi-month holding horizon
data_requirements: point-in-time daily ETF closes and trading calendar
frozen M1 ETF universe and instrument-master identity facts
M0 execution, settlement, fee, and corporate-action facts
pre-registered Basic/OOS date splits and candidate-local benchmarks
